column2: Ravi Ranjan Developers Pvt. Ltd. v. Aditya Kumar Chatterjee
column3: Civil Appeal arising out of SLP (C) Nos. 17397-17398 of 2021
column12: Whether the Calcutta High Court could appoint an arbitrator only because the clause said the tribunal would sit at Kolkata.
column13: No. Kolkata was only a venue for sittings, not the seat; the High Court had no territorial jurisdiction and consent could not give it one.
column14: Mankastu Impex Pvt. Ltd. v. Airvisual Ltd.

column2: BBR (India) Pvt. Ltd. v. S.P. Singla Constructions Pvt. Ltd.
column12: Whether the seat fixed at Panchkula by the first arbitrator moved to Delhi when the substitute arbitrator held hearings there.
column13: No. A seat fixed by the tribunal under s 20(2) stays fixed; later hearings in Delhi were only a change of venue, so the Panchkula courts kept jurisdiction.
column14: BGS SGS Soma JV v. NHPC Ltd.

column2: Gujarat State Civil Supplies Corporation Ltd. v. Mahakali Foods Pvt. Ltd. (Unit 2)
column3: Civil Appeal arising out of SLP (C) No. 12884 of 2020 (with connected appeals)
column12: Whether a private arbitration agreement stops an MSME supplier from taking the dispute to the Facilitation Council under s 18.
column13: No. Chapter V of the MSMED Act overrides the A&C Act and the contract; the Council may conciliate and then arbitrate itself.

column2: Arif Azim Co. Ltd. v. Micromax Informatics FZE
column12: Whether Dubai, called the 'venue' in the clause, was really the seat, which would bar an Indian court from appointing under s 11(6).
column13: Yes. A single named venue with UAE rules and no contrary sign is the seat; Part I does not apply, so the petition failed.
column14: BGS SGS Soma JV v. NHPC Ltd.

column2: Disortho S.A.S. v. Meril Life Sciences Pvt. Ltd.
column12: Whether Indian courts can appoint when one clause chooses Indian law and Gujarat courts and another sends arbitration to a Bogota centre.
column13: Yes. Indian law governs the arbitration agreement, Bogota was not chosen as the seat, so Part I applies; a sole arbitrator was appointed.
column14: Arif Azim Co. Ltd. v. Micromax Informatics FZE

column2: M/s Harcharan Dass Gupta v. Union of India
column12: Whether a Bengaluru seat clause defeats a Delhi MSME supplier's reference by the Delhi Facilitation Council to the Delhi Arbitration Centre.
column13: No. The MSMED Act overrides the agreed seat; the Council where the supplier is located has jurisdiction, and the arbitration was restored.
column14: Gujarat State Civil Supplies Corp. v. Mahakali Foods

column2: M/s Activitas Management Advisor Pvt. Ltd. v. Mind Plus Healthcare Pvt. Ltd.
column3: Civil Appeal arising out of SLP (C) No. 27714 of 2024
column12: Whether a clause giving exclusive jurisdiction to Mumbai courts fixes the seat when the arbitration clause names no seat or venue.
column13: Yes. Read in the context of arbitration, the clause makes Mumbai the seat, so only the Bombay High Court could hear the s 11 application.
column14: Brahmani River Pellets Ltd. v. Kamachi Industries Ltd.

column2: Balaji Steel Trade v. Fludor Benin S.A.
column12: Whether the Supreme Court can appoint an arbitrator for a composite reference when the master agreement says arbitration will take place in Benin.
column13: No. Benin is the seat and Part I does not apply; the later sale contracts did not replace the master agreement, and the petitioner was estopped.
column14: Bharat Aluminium Co. v. Kaiser Aluminium (BALCO)

column2: J&K Economic Reconstruction Agency v. Rash Builders India Pvt. Ltd.
column12: Whether Delhi or Srinagar courts hear the award challenge when the agreed seat was Srinagar but hearings and the award took place in Delhi.
column13: Srinagar. The seat is fixed by agreement and stays fixed; the venue and a recital in the award do not move it. The s 34 petition was restored.
column14: BGS SGS Soma JV v. NHPC Ltd.

column2: Bhartia Infra Projects Ltd. v. M/s Vishwa Samudra Engineering Pvt. Ltd.
column12: Which High Court can appoint when the clause names Hyderabad or Guwahati as seat but gives Hyderabad courts exclusive jurisdiction.
column13: Telangana High Court. The exclusive jurisdiction sentence settles the seat, so Arif Azim's forum non conveniens test for multiple seats is not needed.
column14: Arif Azim Co. Ltd. v. Micromax Informatics FZE
